rows.name: Universe U0

enumeration.datum: Universe carrier U0 — the formation datum: U0 is a type (a closed type constant; the first typed carrier for admissible formation).
enumeration.justification: ADJUDICATED FINAL (undisputed by both audits; upheld). At n=1 the prior ladder is empty, so no class-D construction is available; the datum is a structure, not a law (not P); nothing prior or counted implies its existence (not C); it is not a discrete invariant, clutching class, or gauge choice (not T). Under the Section 4 boundary clause, even granting uniqueness up to canonical isomorphism once postulated, the existence is not implied by prior or counted content, so the existence is the minted content: class N. The contrast with the Stage 8 anchor (carrier class D there) is positional, not a conflict: that carrier is constructible from prior strata; here there are none.

enumeration.datum: Elementhood/decoding — the structural datum interpreting each element a : U0 as an admissible formation candidate: Russell-style rule (from A : U0 infer A type) or, equivalently, the Tarski-style decoding family a : U0 |- El(a) type.
enumeration.justification: ADJUDICATED FINAL (classification undisputed; citation locator amended per completeness audit). Not D: the empty prior ladder supplies no construction of a distinguished family of types over U0. Not C: neither the existence nor the identity of El is implied by the bare carrier or anything prior — a bare type carries no canonical interpretation of its elements as types. Not P: this is generative structure (a dependent family / formation-conferring rule producing new typehood judgments), not a propositional law or coherence condition. Not T: it assigns formation content pointwise; it is no discrete invariant or gauge choice. The analyst's stated doubt (merge with the carrier into one 'type of types' idea) is resolved to two data by the frozen Stage 8 granularity anchor (carrier and operation are separate data) and by the boundary clause (each datum's existence is independently unimplied): class N.

disputes.datum: Elementhood/decoding (datum 2) — citation component: 'Univalent Foundations Program, HoTT (2013), Section 1.3 (Russell-style elementhood; Tarski-style El discussed in the same section)'
disputes.argument: Citation-locator error, verified against the first-edition text (HoTT Book PDF, book pp. 24-25 and 54-55). Section 1.3 'Universes and families' (title verified correct) introduces universes, the U0:U1:U2 hierarchy, cumulativity, typical ambiguity, and type families, but contains NO mention of Tarski-style universes or the El decoding. That discussion is in the Notes to Chapter 1 (book p. 55), which states the book uses 'Russell-style universes' rather than 'Tarski-style universes' in the terminology of [ML84], and describes the explicit coercion El(A) there. The parenthetical 'discussed in the same section' is therefore false; the correct locator is 'HoTT Book, Notes to Chapter 1 (p. 55)'. This is an intra-work mislocation, not a fabricated or wrong-work citation: the content is real, the claim is true, and the datum is independently supported by the analyst's second citation (Martin-Löf 1975, bibliographic details verified exactly: Logic Colloquium '73, ed. Rose & Shepherdson, Studies in Logic 80, North-Holland, 1975, pp. 73-118, the paper that introduced the universe). Classification (N) and D(1)=2 are unaffected; the adjudicator should amend the locator only. All completeness checks otherwise pass: the three enumerated data exhaust the defining data of the bare-universe standard presentation in both Russell and Tarski styles; the positional exclusions (closure codes barred at n=1 with empty prior ladder, hierarchy/cumulativity outside the row reading, judgmental scaffolding as framework presupposition, predicativity as a non-rule) are correct under the frozen rule; no defining datum is missing and no enumerated datum is extraneous.

The frozen rule's Section 4 citation requirement (author, title, chapter/section) is satisfied by amending the locator, which I have done; no classification turns on the locator. Both proposed classes in the dispute were N, so there is nothing to split: datum 2 remains class N under the boundary clause (existence of the decoding is not implied by the bare carrier or the empty prior ladder; its identity-up-to-canonical-isomorphism once postulated does not demote it, because the existence is the minted content). I additionally reviewed the two undisputed classifications against the rule and uphold them: the carrier is N (empty prior ladder at n=1 blocks D; boundary clause governs), and the congruence law is P (pure coherence condition, contributes 0). Final: three defining data, classes N/N/P, D(1) = 2.

rows.name: Unit type 1

enumeration.datum: The unit type former itself: a distinguished admissible type 1 in the universe (formation rule, 1 : U0)
enumeration.justification: Prior content is exactly stratum 1: the universe U0, a typed carrier for admissible formation. A bare carrier of candidates contains no distinguished candidate and supplies no type-forming constructions, so the existence of a first concrete type is not implied by prior content (not D, not C) and the type is a carrier, not classification data or a law (not T, not P). Given existence, a terminal inhabited type is unique up to canonical equivalence, so its identity is canonical; but its existence is not implied. By the Section 4 boundary clause, unique-up-to-canonical-isomorphism given existence with existence not implied is class N: the existence of the first admissible type is the minted content of this stratum.
enumeration.citation: The Univalent Foundations Program, Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics (IAS, 2013), Section 1.5 (unit type introduced as the nullary product) and Appendix A.2 (unit type rules); Per Martin-Lof, Intuitionistic Type Theory (Bibliopolis, 1984), book-level (finite types).

enumeration.datum: Inhabitance specification: the clause 'inhabited' in the reading, i.e., the proposition that 1 has an element
enumeration.justification: Doubt stated: an inhabitant, taken as structure, would be class N since prior content (U0 alone) does not imply the existence of any element. However, on the frozen ladder the explicit term-level realization of inhabitance is verbatim the established reading of stratum 3, one rung later; enumerating the witness as a structural datum of row 2 would mint a later rung's defining datum inside this row and double-count it across the ladder. The datum that belongs to stratum 2's own reading ('terminal inhabited type') is the proof-irrelevant specification that the type is inhabited: a mere propositional clause of the specification. Section 4 places mere properties in class P regardless of whether their truth is implied (compare 'completeness as a property' in the class-P definition). Resolved: P; the structural witness is stratum-3 content, outside this row.

enumeration.datum: Terminality / uniqueness principle (eta): every element of 1 is equal to the canonical one; equivalently, for every admissible type A there is exactly one map A -> 1 (1 is terminal, i.e., contractible once pointed)
enumeration.justification: This is a uniqueness clause / universal property: it constrains the type and its maps but mints no new carrier or operation. Section 4 lists 'uniqueness clauses' explicitly under class P. At this ladder position it is stated judgmentally (maps as terms-in-context over the universe's candidates), not via internal function types (which arrive at stratum 4); either formulation is a propositional law. enumeration.justification: In the standard presentation the introduction rule is an independent primitive: the formation rule of 1 alone yields no term (the empty type has a formation rule of identical shape and no inhabitant), so existence of a witness is not implied by the type former. Given existence, the witness is unique up to canonical identification (any two inhabitants of the null-payload terminal type are canonically equal by stratum 2's uniqueness interface), so the N-vs-C boundary clause governs. Doubt, stated per discipline: stratum 2's verbatim reading contains the descriptor 'inhabited'; if that descriptor were taken as formally realized prior content, the witness's existence would be implied and this datum would be class (C), with d_count 0 for the row. Resolution by the boundary clause and the frozen ladder's own partition of formal contributions: the table assigns 'explicit term-level realization of inhabitance' to stratum 3 as its formal contribution, so the term-level witness cannot simultaneously be stratum 2's realized content (the ladder assigns each contribution to exactly one stratum); stratum 2's 'inhabited' is an interface-level capacity descriptor whose term-level realization is minted here. Note also that no truncation mechanism exists at this ladder position (propositional truncation is stratum 6), so there is no prior device by which 'mere inhabitance' could be held without a witness — confirming that the witness itself is the minted content. Uniqueness-given-existence with existence not implied is class (N): the existence is the minted content. Contributes 1.

enumeration.datum: Σ-formation: the dependent sum former taking A and a family x:A ⊢ B(x) to Σ_{x:A} B(x) in U₀ (dependent pairing as a type-forming structure)
enumeration.justification: A second independent minted structure. Doubt stated and resolved: Σ is not derivable from strata 1..3 nor from the counted Π-former — the impredicative Church-style encoding is unavailable over a predicative U₀ (it lands in a higher universe and fails to yield the dependent eliminator), so existence is not implied by prior or counted content. Unique up to canonical isomorphism whenever it exists (its canonical elements are the dependent pairs; categorically the left-adjoint characterization), existence not implied: boundary clause gives N. enumeration.datum: Pairing (Σ-introduction): from a : A and b : B(a) form (a, b) : Σ_{x:A} B(x)
enumeration.justification: Constitutive canonical-element specification of the counted Σ-former: the standard presentation defines Σ_{x:A} B(x) by prescribing its canonical elements as the pairs (a, b). Given the counted former, existence and identity of the pairing operation are implied, not separately minted. Class C by the boundary clause's second half.

enumeration.datum: Σ-elimination: the induction principle ind_Σ (split), with the projections pr₁, pr₂ as derived instances
enumeration.justification: The non-canonical operation justified by computation on canonical pairs: its identity is fixed by the β-law on pair-forms and its existence is implied by the counted former's definition (elements of the dependent sum are, by the meaning of the type, exhaustively the canonical pairs, which the eliminator consumes). The projections are then defined instances of the eliminator. Existence and identity both implied by counted content: class C.

enumeration.datum: Σ computation rule (β): ind_Σ(C, g, (a, b)) ≡ g(a)(b)
enumeration.justification: Judgmental equational law governing the eliminator against canonical pairs; a coherence condition on already-enumerated data, contributing no structure. Class P.
enumeration.citation: Univalent Foundations Program, Homotopy Type Theory (2013), §1.6 and Appendix A.2; Martin-Löf, Intuitionistic Type Theory (Bibliopolis, 1984) (book-level).

enumeration.datum: Formation rule: the type S1 (in the universe U0)
enumeration.justification: Doubt stated: the existence of a type with a nontrivial generating loop is NOT implied by strata 1-4 (a boundary-clause trigger). The package {formation, base, loop} contains exactly one independent unimplied existence; counting it both here and at loop would double-count one minted idea, violating the Section 3 independence requirement. The row reading fixes the mint's location at the path constructor ('first nontrivial path constructor'), so formation is class C. Contributes 0.

enumeration.datum: Point constructor: base : S1
enumeration.justification: The point-constructor pattern is prior content: stratum 3 mints term-level witnesses (star : 1), and the sub-presentation generated by base alone — the free type on one point constructor — is canonically the unit type (1, star) of strata 2-3. base introduces no new structural kind; it is the prior point-generation pattern reused inside the new specification. Doubt noted between D and C (as part of the generated package its identity is also implied by the specification); both are zero classes, and D is chosen because the underlying object (the pointed 0-skeleton) is constructible verbatim from strata 2-3 content. Not N in either case. Contributes 0.
enumeration.citation: Univalent Foundations Program, Homotopy Type Theory (2013), Ch. 1, Sec. 1.5 (Product types / unit type) and Ch. 6, Sec. 6.4

enumeration.datum: Path constructor: loop : base =_{S1} base (the generating loop)
enumeration.justification: The single minted idea of the stratum. A constructor targeting an identity type of the type being generated is a new structural kind with no precedent in strata 1-4: the prior ladder (U0, 1, star, Pi/Sigma with transport) supplies only reflexivity paths and no mechanism to adjoin a generating non-trivial loop; adjoining loop changes the generated carrier from (the unit type) to the circle. Boundary clause applied: the generated package is unique up to canonical equivalence whenever it exists, but its existence is not implied by prior or previously counted content — the existence is the minted content, hence N. This datum is verbatim the row's established reading ('first nontrivial path constructor and topological generator'). Contributes 1.
enumeration.citation: Univalent Foundations Program, Homotopy Type Theory (2013), Ch. 6, Secs. 6.1 and 6.4 (the circle as the higher inductive type generated by base and loop)

enumeration.datum: Induction principle (dependent eliminator): for P : S1 -> U, given b : P(base) and a dependent path l : b =^P_{loop} b, a section f : Pi(x:S1) P(x)
enumeration.justification: Doubt stated between N and P; resolved as P, not by convenience but by the standard mathematical content: the induction principle (with propositional computation rules) is equivalent to homotopy-initiality of the algebra (S1, base, loop), and homotopy-initiality is a mere proposition — a universal property, not independently variable structure. It is the propositional unfolding of the already-counted generator datum: a 'generating' loop without its universal property is not a generator, so induction cannot be varied independently of the counted mint. This matches the Section 5 stage-8 anchor pattern (one operation N, its coherence/discipline P). The statement's dependent-path apparatus (apd, transport) is prior stratum-4 content. Caveat recorded in notes: the propositionality theorem uses function extensionality. Contributes 0.
enumeration.citation: K. Sojakova, 'Higher Inductive Types as Homotopy-Initial Algebras', POPL 2015; S. Awodey, N. Gambino, K. Sojakova, 'Inductive Types in Homotopy Type Theory', LICS 2012; Univalent Foundations Program, Homotopy Type Theory (2013), Ch. 6, Sec. 6.2

enumeration.datum: Recursion principle (simple eliminator): for a type A with a : A and p : a = a, a map f : S1 -> A with f(base) = a and ap_f(loop) = p
enumeration.justification: Existence and identity are both implied by counted/enumerated content: recursion is the specialization of the induction principle to constant families (dependent paths over constant families reduce to ordinary paths via prior stratum-4 transport). A quantity mechanically derived from data already enumerated — the paradigm C case. Contributes 0.
enumeration.citation: Univalent Foundations Program, Homotopy Type Theory (2013), Ch. 6, Secs. 6.2 and 6.4 (recursion derived from induction via constant families)

enumeration.datum: Computation rule for base: f(base) == b (judgmental beta-rule of the eliminator at the point constructor)
enumeration.justification: A propositional/equational law: a coherence condition tying the eliminator's value at the point generator to the supplied datum. It is a demanded equation on already-enumerated operations, exactly the 'coherence condition / law' case of class P (compare the stage-8 anchor, where the H-space coherence pattern is P). Contributes 0.

enumeration.datum: Computation rule for loop: apd_f(loop) = l (propositional beta-rule of the eliminator at the path constructor)
enumeration.justification: A propositional equation (explicitly propositional, not judgmental, in the standard presentation): the coherence law tying the eliminator to the path generator, stated with the apd/dependent-path apparatus derived from stratum-4 transport. A law on already-enumerated operations; class P. Contributes 0.

rows.notes: Standard presentation used: the circle as the higher inductive type generated by one point constructor and one path constructor, with induction and computation rules (HoTT Book, Ch. 6). Prior-content assumptions relied on: identity types with transport and dependent-path (apd) machinery are stratum-4 content per that row's 'interface transport over terms'; the point-generation pattern with eliminator is strata 2-3 content. Single-mint placement: the package {formation, base, loop} carries exactly one unimplied existence; per Section 3 independence and the row's own reading ('first nontrivial path constructor'), it is located at loop and counted once — an auditor relocating it to the formation rule leaves d_count unchanged at 1. Induction-as-P caveat: the theorem that induction with propositional computation rules is equivalent to homotopy-initiality (a mere proposition) is proved in type theory assuming function extensionality (Sojakova, POPL 2015, covering W-suspensions including the circle); funext is not explicitly listed in strata 1-4, so if the eventual adjudicator rejects the initiality reading, the fallback classification for the induction principle is C (form mechanically determined by the constructor signature under the generation scheme, existence bundled with the counted generation act) — also a zero class, leaving d_count = 1 in either case. The classification that WOULD change the count is treating induction as an independent N (d_count 2); this was considered and rejected because a generating constructor and its universal property are not independently variable primitives, matching the stage-8 anchor's bundling of an operation with its coherence pattern. Not enumerated (theorems/consequences, not defining data): nontriviality loop != refl (requires univalence, a model-level fact), pi_1(S1) = Z, S1 = free infinity-groupoid on one automorphism, equivalence with suspension presentations. Calibration consistency: carrier/point data zero-classed as in the stage-9 anchor (carrier D), determined derivates zero-classed as in stage 12 (C), single operation minted as in stage 8 (N with coherence P). d_count = 1.

rows.name: Propositional truncation

enumeration.datum: Truncation type former (formation rule): for each type A, the type ‖A‖ — the reflection of A into mere propositions
enumeration.justification: The stratum's single minted primitive: proof-irrelevant compression as a type former. Existence is NOT implied by prior content (U0, 1, star, Pi/Sigma, S1): the ladder below contains no quotient-like or general higher-inductive machinery — stratum 5 mints one specific type with one specific loop constructor, not a HIT scheme, and the known reductions of propositional truncation to other colimits (hub-and-spoke, iterated joins via pushouts) use higher inductive types not on the ladder; the impredicative encoding Pi(P:Prop).(A->P)->P raises universe level and only yields the truncation under propositional resizing, which is not prior content. Given the other enumerated data (unit, prop-ness, universal property), ‖A‖ is determined up to canonical equivalence whenever it exists; by the Section 4 boundary clause the unimplied existence is exactly the minted content: class N.
enumeration.citation: The Univalent Foundations Program, Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics (IAS, 2013), §3.7 (Propositional truncation) and §6.9 (Truncations)

enumeration.datum: Point constructor (unit map): |–| : A → ‖A‖
enumeration.justification: Existence and identity are both implied by counted content. Existence: datum 1 is counted as the reflection of A into mere propositions, whose specification includes its unit map — the mint of the (former, unit) package is charged exactly once, at datum 1. Identity: since ‖A‖ is a mere proposition (squash datum), any two maps A → ‖A‖ are pointwise propositionally equal, so the unit admits no independent choice — it is canonically determined. Doubt stated: on a bare-HIT reading the point constructor is co-postulated with the formation rule and could look like separate structure; but co-postulation inside a single inference package is precisely 'existence implied by other counted data', and the boundary clause therefore sends it to C, not N. Counting it N as well would double-count one minted idea, contrary to the Section 3 granularity fixed by the stage-8 anchor (one operation, one mint).
enumeration.citation: The Univalent Foundations Program, Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics (IAS, 2013), §3.7 (Propositional truncation); canonical identity of maps into a mere proposition per §3.3 (Mere propositions)

enumeration.datum: Path constructor (squash / proof irrelevance): for all x, y : ‖A‖, x = y — i.e., is-prop(‖A‖)
enumeration.justification: A propositional law about the counted carrier: is-prop(X) is itself a mere proposition, so this datum is a mere property / coherence condition, the exact pattern the rule assigns to class P and the stage-8 anchor assigns to the H-space coherence. The predicate itself is expressible from prior content (Pi over the ambient identity types that stratum 5 already presupposes). Its existence-content — that a former with this property exists at all — is not carried here: that is the mint already charged at datum 1. Class P, contributes 0.
enumeration.citation: The Univalent Foundations Program, Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics (IAS, 2013), §3.7 (Propositional truncation); §3.3 (Mere propositions: being a mere proposition is itself a mere proposition)

enumeration.datum: Recursion principle (universal property): for every mere proposition B, every f : A → B extends along |–| to g : ‖A‖ → B — equivalently, precomposition (‖A‖ → B) → (A → B) is an equivalence
enumeration.justification: A universal characterization, which the rule classes with 'uniqueness clauses' and 'completeness as a property'. Because B is a mere proposition, the type of extensions of f along |–| is itself a mere proposition (any two extensions are pointwise equal), and 'precomposition is an equivalence' is a mere proposition; so this datum is a propositional law characterizing datum 1, not new structure. Doubt stated: an eliminator can be read as a structural rule; but its content over propositional targets is propositional, and its existence-content is exactly what the boundary clause consumed at datum 1 (uniqueness-given-existence there, existence minted there) — charging it again here would double-count. Class P.
enumeration.citation: The Univalent Foundations Program, Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics (IAS, 2013), §3.7 (Propositional truncation) and §6.9 (Truncations)

enumeration.datum: Computation rule: rec(f)(|a|) ≡ f(a)
enumeration.justification: A coherence equation attached to the recursion principle. Propositionally it is automatic: both sides inhabit the mere proposition B and are therefore equal; as a judgmental clause it is a law governing already-enumerated data, not an independent structural primitive. Class P (coherence condition), contributes 0.
enumeration.citation: The Univalent Foundations Program, Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics (IAS, 2013), §3.7 (Propositional truncation) and §6.9 (Truncations)

enumeration.datum: Dependent induction principle: for B : ‖A‖ → U with each B(x) a mere proposition, (Π(a:A) B(|a|)) → Π(x:‖A‖) B(x)
enumeration.justification: Existence and identity are both implied by other counted data: it is derivable from the recursion principle together with the squash path constructor (the standard derivation of truncation induction for families of mere propositions), and its value is unique because each fiber B(x) is a mere proposition. Enumerated for completeness of the standard presentation; class C, contributes 0.
enumeration.citation: The Univalent Foundations Program, Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics (IAS, 2013), §6.9 (Truncations)

rows.name: Sphere S2

enumeration.datum: Carrier type S² : U (type formation of the sphere as a homotopy type)
enumeration.justification: The carrier is not constructible from strata 1..6 by available constructions (the prior ladder has Π/Σ, the circle's 1-dimensional generator, and truncation, but no suspension/pushout/HIT-former machinery), so it is not (D). Doubt stated: one could read the carrier as (N). Resolved by the boundary clause: the carrier's existence and identity are both implied by the datum counted as (N) below — the free attachment of a 2-cell — since the freely generated type is determined up to canonical equivalence by its generation data via its universal property, and the existence assertion lives entirely in that counted generator. Existence and identity both implied by counted content = (C). Counting the carrier as well would double-count the single minted idea, violating the minted-idea granularity (Section 3) and the stage-8 anchor pattern in which the carrier is a zero class while the stratum's one new structure carries the count.

enumeration.datum: Point constructor base : S² (basepoint / unique 0-cell)
enumeration.justification: The pointedness datum reproduces prior-ladder content at minted-idea granularity: stratum 3 mints the term-level witness idea (⋆ : 1, explicit realization of inhabitance) and stratum 5's presentation already contains a point constructor for a generated carrier. The basepoint of S² adds no structural idea not already present below; it is the zero-dimensional component of the presentation, and Section 3 forbids counting components. Doubt stated: literally, base is a generator of a new type, not a term built from prior strata; but the (D)/(N) question is decided at minted-idea granularity, and the idea 'distinguished witness point of a carrier' is fully prior. In CW terms this is the single 0-cell, a copy of the terminal cell already available from stratum 2/3 content.

enumeration.justification: This is the stratum's minted idea: the first generator living in an iterated identity type — free attachment of a two-dimensional cell. Its existence is not implied by strata 1..6: the prior ladder contains exactly one nontrivial path generator (loop, dimension 1, stratum 5) and the truncation squash (stratum 6, which compresses rather than generates), and no suspension, pushout, or general cell-attachment former from which a 2-cell could be built. Boundary clause applied: given existence, the type freely generated by base and surf is unique up to canonical equivalence (universal property), but that existence is exactly what is minted here — unique-up-to-canonical-iso GIVEN existence with existence not implied is (N). This single datum carries the 'surface coherence' capacity of the row input.

enumeration.datum: Boundary specification of the 2-cell: source and target of surf are both refl_base (classically, the attaching map S¹ → {e⁰} is the constant map)

Existence and identity are both implied by prior and counted content, so (C). enumeration.datum: Shape modality SHAPE (Pi_infinity, fundamental infinity-groupoid): idempotent monadic modal operator A |-> SHAPE A with unit A -> SHAPE A, reflecting a cohesive type onto a discrete type; externally SHAPE = Disc o Pi_infinity
enumeration.justification: New operator. Stated doubt: given FLAT one may argue SHAPE is 'the left adjoint of FLAT', unique up to canonical isomorphism, suggesting C; but existence of that left adjoint is not implied by FLAT or SHARP -- external witness: local but not locally infinity-connected toposes have FLAT and SHARP but no SHAPE (local infinity-connectedness is an independent condition on geometric morphisms). This is precisely the boundary-clause case: unique up to canonical isomorphism whenever it exists, existence not implied, hence N -- the existence is the minted content. (In real-cohesion SHAPE is constructed as nullification at the reals, but the reals are later/physical content, not prior ladder content; the abstract package postulates SHAPE.) Contributes 1.

enumeration.datum: Codiscrete subuniverse and its inclusion coDisc: the class of codiscrete types (those A with A -> SHARP A an equivalence) and its embedding
enumeration.justification: Existence and identity implied by the counted datum SHARP: codiscrete types are the SHARP-modal fixed points; the inclusion is canonically determined. Contributes 0.

enumeration.justification: A mere property of the counted operator SHAPE (a condition that certain canonical comparison maps are equivalences). It constrains but does not add structure. Contributes 0.

rows.notes: Presentation choice: since the ladder's strata 1..9 are internal type-theoretic content (universe, unit, witness, Pi/Sigma, S1, truncation, S2, S3 H-space, Hopf), the stratum's standard presentation is taken to be axiomatic cohesive homotopy type theory (Schreiber-Shulman; Shulman's crisp modal type theory), with the external cohesive infinity-topos quadruple Pi_infinity -| Disc -| Gamma -| coDisc (Lawvere; Schreiber) used as the semantic counterpart in justifications. Under this reading the package mints exactly three independent structural primitives: the operators FLAT, SHARP, SHAPE. Their independence is witnessed semantically: FLAT alone (any topos over a base has Disc, Gamma), SHARP requires locality (fails e.g. for sheaves on the real line), SHAPE requires local infinity-connectedness (fails for local but non-locally-connected toposes) -- three separate existence axioms. All adjoint relations, idempotency/(co)monad laws, full-faithfulness, and product preservation are classed P; the discrete/codiscrete subuniverses, the Gamma factorization, and the crisp-context apparatus are classed C. The carrier is classed D (the prior type theory itself; no new ambient object is minted internally). Key boundary-clause resolutions recorded inside the entries: SHAPE and SHARP are each unique up to canonical isomorphism as adjoints GIVEN existence, but their existence is not implied by prior or counted content, so each is N (the existence is the mint); the external canonicity argument for FLAT presupposes the base-of-discretes structure that this stratum itself introduces, so FLAT is N. Granularity cross-checked against the Stage-8 anchor (carrier D, operation N, coherence P): here carrier D, three operators N, laws P. No datum of class T arises. Citations are given at paper/book level where section numbers could not be asserted with certainty (per the no-fabrication rule); no local files were read and no Column-S or register content was consulted. d_count = 3 (FLAT, SHARP, SHAPE).

rows.name: Connection shell

enumeration.datum: Carrier: the cohesive family/fibration pi: E -> M (principal or associated bundle with cohesive fibers) on which transport is to act
enumeration.justification: The underlying family is constructible from prior ladder content: dependent families and their interface transport over terms (stratum 4, Pi/Sigma shell), concrete bundle instances (stratum 9, Hopf fibration), and cohesive structure on families (stratum 10, modal shell). No new carrier is minted at this stratum. This matches the frozen stage-9 anchor, which classes the bundle carrier itself as (D).
enumeration.citation: Kobayashi & Nomizu, Foundations of Differential Geometry, Vol. I, Ch. I, Sec. 5 (Fibre bundles)

enumeration.datum: Vertical subbundle V = ker(d pi) of TE (the tangent-to-the-fiber distribution)
enumeration.justification: Existence and identity are both implied by the carrier: the vertical subspace at each point is canonically the kernel of the differential of the projection (equivalently, the tangent space of the fiber through that point). Nothing is chosen; it is computed from counted/prior data. Class (C) by the boundary clause since both existence and identity are implied.
enumeration.citation: Kobayashi & Nomizu, Foundations of Differential Geometry, Vol. I, Ch. II, Sec. 1 (Connections in a principal fibre bundle)

enumeration.datum: Domain of comparison: the smooth path groupoid P1(M) (paths up to thin homotopy / reparametrization) over which fibers are compared
enumeration.justification: Constructible from prior ladder content: path/loop structure is available from stratum 5 (path constructor) and the cohesive shape infrastructure of stratum 10; classically it is built from the manifold carrier by standard constructions available below this rung. It is the stage on which transport acts, not a minted structure of this stratum.
enumeration.citation: Schreiber & Waldorf, Parallel Transport and Functors, Journal of Homotopy and Related Structures 4 (2009) (article-level; section uncertain)

enumeration.datum: The connection nabla itself: a G-equivariant horizontal distribution H in TE complementary to V, equivalently the g-valued connection 1-form omega, equivalently the covariant derivative operator on sections, equivalently the smooth transport functor on P1(M) — one structural primitive presented four equivalent ways
enumeration.justification: This is the single minted idea of the stratum. Doubt stated and resolved: existence of SOME connection on a bundle over a paracompact base is a theorem (K&N Ch. II Sec. 2), so one might attempt (C); but class (C) requires existence AND identity to be implied, and identity is not — the set of connections is a nonempty affine space modeled on ad-bundle-valued 1-forms with no canonical point, and distinct connections are observably distinct structures (they induce different fiber comparisons). Not (T): the choice is not pure gauge and has local content. Not (P): it is a structure, not a law. Not (D): no construction from strata 1..10 produces a distinguished nabla on a general cohesive family; stratum 10's flat modality distinguishes only the flat/discrete comparison, against which a general nabla is precisely the non-implied datum. By the boundary clause the existence/choice is the minted content: class (N). Granularity per Section 3 and the stage-8 anchor: horizontal distribution, connection form, covariant derivative, and transport functor are canonically equivalent presentations of one primitive and are counted once, exactly as the H-space anchor counts one operation.
enumeration.citation: Kobayashi & Nomizu, Foundations of Differential Geometry, Vol. I, Ch. II, Secs. 1-2 (Connections in a principal fibre bundle; Existence and extension of connections)

enumeration.datum: Connection laws: reproduction omega(A*) = A and equivariance R_a* omega = Ad(a^{-1}) omega of the connection form; equivalently G-invariance and smoothness of H; equivalently additivity, C-infinity-linearity in the direction argument, and the Leibniz rule for the covariant derivative
enumeration.justification: These are propositional laws/coherence conditions imposed on the already-counted datum nabla, not new structure: they cut out which candidate distributions/forms/operators qualify as connections. Mere properties contribute 0, mirroring the stage-8 anchor where the coherence pattern of the counted operation is class (P).
enumeration.citation: Kobayashi & Nomizu, Foundations of Differential Geometry, Vol. I, Ch. II, Sec. 1 (Connections in a principal fibre bundle)

enumeration.datum: Parallel transport P_gamma: E_{gamma(0)} -> E_{gamma(1)} along paths — the comparison of cohesive fibers named in the established reading
enumeration.justification: Given the counted datum nabla, horizontal lifts of paths exist and are unique (standard existence/uniqueness for the horizontal-lift equation), so the fiber-comparison maps exist and are canonically determined by nabla; both existence and identity are implied by counted content, hence (C), not (N). This is the same determination pattern the stage-12 anchor freezes for curvature relative to nabla. The reading's 'parallel transport and comparison of cohesive fibers' therefore carries no independent count beyond the connection itself.
enumeration.citation: Kobayashi & Nomizu, Foundations of Differential Geometry, Vol. I, Ch. II, Sec. 3 (Parallelism)

enumeration.datum: Transport coherence: functoriality under path composition and reversal, invariance under reparametrization/thin homotopy, and smooth dependence on the path (the smooth-functor condition)
enumeration.justification: These are coherence laws satisfied by the determined transport (equivalently, the axioms making the transport presentation a smooth functor); they are properties of already-counted data and mint no structure. Under the equivalence of presentations they correspond to the connection laws already classed (P) and are listed separately only for completeness of the transport-side presentation.
enumeration.citation: Schreiber & Waldorf, Parallel Transport and Functors, Journal of Homotopy and Related Structures 4 (2009) (article-level; section uncertain)

enumeration.datum: Flat/discrete comparison object: the flat-modality counterpart of the family (flat coefficient / de Rham-style comparison object built from the stratum-10 adjunction), against which nabla is read as 'acting on cohesive families'
enumeration.justification: In the cohesive presentation, the flat comparison object is constructed canonically by applying the stratum-10 modal adjunction (Pi-infinity -| Disc -| flat -| sharp) to prior carriers: existence and identity are both implied by prior strata, with no choice. It supplies the ambient notion of trivial/flat transport; the non-implied deviation from it is exactly the datum already counted as (N).
enumeration.citation: Schreiber, Differential Cohomology in a Cohesive Infinity-Topos, arXiv:1310.7930 (document-level; section uncertain)

Presentation chosen: the standard Ehresmann/Kobayashi-Nomizu principal-bundle presentation, supplemented by the transport-functor presentation (Schreiber-Waldorf) and the cohesive framing (Schreiber) demanded by the row's 'cohesive families' language; these are canonically equivalent, and per Section 3 granularity the horizontal distribution / connection form / covariant derivative / transport functor are counted as ONE primitive. The single class-N datum is the connection nabla itself; the decisive boundary-clause application is recorded inside that datum: an existence theorem for SOME connection does not imply identity (nonempty affine space of choices, no canonical point, choices not pure gauge since transports differ observably), so the choice is the minted content. rows.name: Curvature shell

enumeration.datum: Carrier space of curvature: bundle-valued 2-forms Omega^2(M; End(E)) (equivalently ad(P)-valued 2-forms on a principal bundle)
enumeration.justification: The space in which R_nabla lives is assembled entirely from prior-ladder content: dependent/pair formers and interface transport (stratum 4) give the endomorphism/associated-bundle construction, the cohesive/modal shell (stratum 10) supplies the infinitesimal-form apparatus, and the connection shell (stratum 11) supplies the bundle-with-transport it is built over. No new carrier is minted at stratum 12; the object is constructible at ladder position 11.
enumeration.citation: Kobayashi & Nomizu, Foundations of Differential Geometry, Vol. I, Chapter II (Theory of Connections), Section 5 (Curvature form and structure equation)

enumeration.datum: Exterior covariant derivative d^nabla extending nabla to bundle-valued forms (the operator whose square, or whose structure-equation combination, is the curvature)
enumeration.justification: Doubt stated: this is an operation, so one must ask whether it is a minted structural primitive. Resolution by the boundary clause: given nabla (stratum 11) and the graded wedge/differential structure on forms (prior content), d^nabla is the unique extension satisfying the graded Leibniz rule d^nabla(omega tensor s) = d omega tensor s + (-1)^k omega wedge nabla s. Both its existence and its identity are implied by prior and previously-counted content, with no free choice; hence class C, not N.
enumeration.citation: Milnor & Stasheff, Characteristic Classes, Appendix C (Connections, Curvature, and Characteristic Classes)

enumeration.datum: The curvature form itself, R_nabla = d nabla + nabla wedge nabla (equivalently F = dA + A wedge A, the second structure equation; equivalently R_nabla = (d^nabla)^2; equivalently R(X,Y) = nabla_X nabla_Y - nabla_Y nabla_X - nabla_[X,Y])
enumeration.justification: The headline datum of the stratum. Its existence AND identity are both implied: R_nabla is computed by a closed formula from the connection nabla counted at stratum 11 and from prior differential/wedge structure. It is exactly the rule's paradigm case of 'a quantity computed by a formula from counted data'. No independent existence is minted -- every connection has a curvature, automatically and canonically. Class C. This agrees with the disclosed Stage-12 calibration anchor, but the classification here is derived independently from the boundary clause: existence is implied, so the N-boundary clause does not fire.
enumeration.citation: Kobayashi & Nomizu, Foundations of Differential Geometry, Vol. I, Chapter II (Theory of Connections), Section 5 (Curvature form and structure equation)

enumeration.datum: Tensoriality of curvature: R_nabla is C-infinity-bilinear in its vector-field arguments, i.e. a genuine 2-form with values in End(E), despite being built from differential operators
enumeration.justification: A propositional fact about the already-determined object R_nabla (first-order derivative terms cancel). It adds no structure; it is a property verified of datum 3. Class P.
enumeration.citation: Tu, Differential Geometry: Connections, Curvature, and Characteristic Classes (Springer GTM 275), chapters on connections and curvature (book-level; exact section numbering not certified)

enumeration.datum: The (second) Bianchi identity: d^nabla R_nabla = 0 (equivalently dF + [A, F] = 0)
enumeration.justification: A coherence law automatically satisfied by the curvature of any connection; it is a proposition proved from data already enumerated (data 2 and 3), minting nothing. Class P.
enumeration.citation: Kobayashi & Nomizu, Foundations of Differential Geometry, Vol. I, Chapter II (Theory of Connections), Section 5 (Curvature form and structure equation)

enumeration.datum: Gauge naturality of curvature: under a gauge transformation g the curvature transforms equivariantly, F mapsto Ad_{g^{-1}} F (tensorially), in contrast to the affine transformation law of the connection
enumeration.justification: A naturality/equivariance law -- a propositional square commuting for the already-determined assignment nabla mapsto R_nabla. Properties and naturality squares are explicitly zero-class under Section 4. Class P.
enumeration.citation: Kobayashi & Nomizu, Foundations of Differential Geometry, Vol. I, Chapter II (Theory of Connections), Section 6 (Mappings of connections) and Section 5 (book-level fallback for the transformation law)

enumeration.datum: Loop-defect reading: curvature measures the infinitesimal holonomy defect of parallel transport around small loops; transport around the boundary of a small parallelogram deviates from the identity at second order exactly by R_nabla, and the holonomy Lie algebra is generated by curvature values (Ambrose-Singer)
enumeration.justification: This is the stratum's established reading ('loop-defect measurement for connection transport'), and it is a theorem ABOUT the pair (nabla, R_nabla), not an additional structural datum: it identifies the already-counted formula-object of datum 3 with the loop defect of the stratum-11 transport. A theorem relating counted data to prior content is propositional. Class P.
enumeration.citation: Kobayashi & Nomizu, Foundations of Differential Geometry, Vol. I, Chapter II (Theory of Connections), Section 8 (Holonomy theorem; Ambrose-Singer)

enumeration.datum: Flatness as the distinguished vanishing condition: R_nabla = 0 if and only if parallel transport is locally path-independent (local triviality of transport)
enumeration.justification: A mere condition on the determined object R_nabla together with an equivalence theorem; it selects a subclass of stratum-11 connections and mints no new structure. Class P.
enumeration.citation: Kobayashi & Nomizu, Foundations of Differential Geometry, Vol. I, Chapter II (Theory of Connections), Section 9 (Flat connections)

enumeration.datum: Underlying smooth/cohesive carrier M
enumeration.justification: The carrier space is prior content: strata 10-12 (cohesion, connection, curvature) already operate on it, and the standard presentation of Riemannian geometry begins 'let M be a smooth manifold' with the manifold given. enumeration.datum: Tangent bundle TM (equivalently the de Rham cotangent/forms carrier on which g will live)
enumeration.justification: TM is a canonical functorial construction from the smooth carrier, with no choice content; moreover differential forms and the exterior derivative d are already in play at stratum 12 (its signature R_nabla = d nabla + nabla wedge nabla uses d and wedge), so the (co)tangent apparatus is available prior content. enumeration.datum: Riemannian metric g (smooth family of inner products on the fibers of TM)
enumeration.justification: The single minted idea of the stratum. Nothing in strata 1..12 implies a metric: a cohesive carrier with connection and curvature machinery carries no preferred fiberwise inner product. Doubt stated and resolved: (i) on a paracompact manifold metrics always exist by partitions of unity, but that existence is a theorem about an auxiliary choice, not existence implied by prior or counted ladder content, and (ii) a metric is radically non-unique with no canonical identity, so class (C) fails on both prongs. It is structure with genuine local content (not a law, not discrete, not a mere carrier), hence (N) under the boundary clause.

enumeration.justification: A propositional law constraining the counted tensor g, exactly parallel to the Stage 8 anchor where the H-space coherence pattern is class (P). Contributes no structure.

enumeration.justification: A mere property (an open condition) on the counted datum g, not an independent structure. The discrete choice of signature, if enumerated separately, would be class (T); it is folded into this axiom clause and contributes 0 either way.

disputes.datum: Next/later modality package (Next : U -> U with unit next and applicative action)
disputes.argument: The N-justification ('no prior stratum implies the existence of a temporal endomodality') is contradicted by the analyst's own datum 2, which classes the carrier as the topos-of-trees construction 'formed from strata 1..14 content by constructions already available there' (class D). On that filed carrier — families over the D-classed clock omega with restriction maps, built by stratum-4 Pi/Sigma over the stratum-1 universe — the later modality is computed by the canonical shift formula: (Next A)(0) = 1, (Next A)(n+1) = A(n), with the unit next given by the restriction maps and the applicative action defined pointwise. This is exactly how the analyst's own primary citation (Birkedal et al., LMCS 8(4), 2012) introduces the modality in the topos of trees: by definition on the derived carrier, not as an axiom. Existence AND identity are therefore implied by prior strata plus already-enumerated data — the anchor-12 pattern verbatim ('a quantity computed by a formula from counted data'), class C. The anchor-8 escape (derived carrier, N operation) is unavailable: at stage 8 no multiplication is derivable from strata 1-7, whereas here derivability of the entire apparatus is asserted by the analyst's own data 1-2 justifications (omega with its induction extractable from stratum-13/14 numeric infrastructure, which is needed to even state those packages and therefore includes classical N-induction, sufficient to define the shift by omega-recursion). The only rescue is the synthetic-axiomatic reading (Nakano/Clouston: a primitive modality on the ambient universe, non-conservative over strata 1-14, hence genuinely N) — but that reading contradicts datum 2 as filed, which states the modalities act on the derived presheaf carrier. The enumeration cannot hold both readings simultaneously; as filed, the C-clause applies.

disputes.datum: Guarded fixpoint operator fix : (Next A -> A) -> A (Loeb principle)
disputes.argument: Same internal inconsistency, applied to fix. On the carrier as filed in datum 2 (topos of trees over the D-classed clock), fix is definable by omega-induction: fix(f) at stage 0 is f applied to the trivial approximation, and at stage n+1 is f applied to the shifted stage-n value — precisely the step-indexing construction named in the title of the analyst's own citation ('step-indexing in the topos of trees'), where the guarded fixed-point combinator and the validity of the Loeb rule are theorems constructed from the presheaf structure, not postulates. The analyst's independence argument — 'pointed applicative endomodalities without a Loeb rule exist, so nothing prior or counted forces fix' — establishes only that the abstract Next package does not force fix. But the frozen C-test is 'existence and identity are implied by prior strata or by other data already counted', and the already-enumerated datum 2 carrier does imply it (given the omega-eliminator that datum 1's own D-justification must supply, since classical stratum-13/14 mathematics includes N-induction). Identity is conceded by the analyst in datum 6 (uniqueness of guarded fixed points). Existence and identity both implied: class C under the boundary clause as written. As with Next, fix is N only under the synthetic-ambient-universe presentation, which the filed datum 2 excludes.

disputes.datum: Eventually modality (Eventually : U -> U with unit)
disputes.argument: The N-classification fails on a dilemma between the analyst's own cited presentations. Horn 1: under the presentation actually cited as standard for this datum (Jeffrey, 'LTL types FRP', PLPV 2012), temporal types are families over the time index and Eventually is a Sigma-construction over future indices — a formula built from stratum-4 Sigma over the D-classed clock, with its unit the evident inclusion at the current index. Existence and identity are both implied by prior/counted content: class C (or D), not N; in Jeffrey's system the LTL modalities are defined, never minted. Horn 2: under the guarded/step-indexed carrier actually filed as datum 2 (topos of trees), the analyst's own argument (via Atkey-McBride) shows the genuine liveness modality is NOT available without clock-quantifier/constant-type machinery, which the analyst explicitly excludes as outside the frozen signature — so on the filed carrier there is no lawful independent Eventually to enumerate at all, and its N-classification tacitly switches to a third presentation (synthetic temporal type theory on the ambient universe) inconsistent with datum 2 as filed. On either horn the filed class-N assignment with its stated justification does not survive; on the reading consistent with the analyst's own carrier and citations, the datum is C.

Counter-direction audit result, recorded because this classification is load-bearing for the whole row rather than harmlessly zero. If the D-justification is upheld — omega extractable from stratum-13/14 numeric infrastructure — then that infrastructure is classical and necessarily carries N-induction (one cannot have the (H, B(H), Spec) package as established content without the numeric tower and its recursion), which supplies the omega-eliminator and triggers the C-cascade of the three disputes above, driving the row toward D(15) = 0. If instead the extraction claim is rejected on the ground that the frozen prior content is only the listed formal contributions of strata 1-14 — which presuppose but do not contain a natural-numbers object with its eliminator, no stratum ever having minted one — then omega is itself an unimplied new independent structure (class N, the minted time order), and Next/fix/Eventually become C relative to it, giving D(15) = 1. The filed d_count = 3 is reachable only under a third resolution: the synthetic-axiomatic reading in which the modalities are primitive structure on the ambient universe — a reading arguably matching the row signature's package style, but one that requires refiling datum 2, whose current description ('the carrier on which the temporal modalities act is formed from strata 1..14 content') contradicts it. In no resolution does the enumeration as filed stand with all of its own justifications intact; the adjudicator must fix the standard presentation first and refile the affected classifications consistently.

adjudication.resolution: Root resolution — presentation fix: Section 4 counts the defining data of the stratum's standard presentation of the frozen reading, and the reading is 'guarded temporal modalities and cohesive exchange laws' (signature: Next, Eventually, cohesive exchange, guarded coherence). Its standard presentation is the synthetic/internal one (Nakano; Clouston et al., whose syntax has later/next/applicative-action/fix as primitives and no clock object), consistent with the ladder's own synthetic character (stratum 10 mints its modal quadruple axiomatically on the ambient type theory). The topos of trees is the model of the presentation, not the presentation. The independence audit correctly identified that the analyst's datum 2, as filed in model-theoretic language, contradicted the N-classifications; the rule-dictated cure is to refile datum 2 (carrier = ambient cohesive universe, class D preserved), not to flip the modalities to C on the strength of a mis-filed carrier description. Second, the audit's C-cascade fails even on its own model reading: the shift formula for Next, step-indexed fix, and Sigma-over-future-indices Eventually all require an internal clock plus universe-valued (large) recursion over it, and the Section 2 cumulativity clause fixes prior content to the listed formal contributions of strata 1..14 — no stratum minted a natural-numbers object, an eliminator, coproducts, or large recursion. The audit's extraction of N-induction from the stratum-13/14 analytic packages reads presupposed classical meta-theory as content; under that collapse-reading arbitrary classical constructions become 'available at that ladder point' and the counting discipline voids at every analytic stratum, so it is rejected: presupposition is not content. Dispute 1 (Next, N->C): C rejected, N upheld — existence not implied by prior strata (stratum-6/10 modalities are idempotent, Next is not) nor by counted data (refiled clock supplies no eliminator); unique-when-exists; boundary clause mints the existence. Dispute 2 (fix, N->C): C rejected, N upheld — step-indexing derivation unlawful as above; pointed applicative delay without Loeb exists (Loeb encodes the models' well-foundedness, genuinely additional content), so the counted Next package does not imply fix; identity half is datum 6's uniqueness; boundary clause verbatim. Dispute 3 (Eventually, N->C-or-delete): both horns rejected — horn 1 is the unavailable model reading (and the internal fixpoint route lacks coproducts and type-level fix); horn 2 would delete a frozen signature item, which the adjudicator cannot do; Atkey-McBride non-derivability of liveness in the guarded fragment is the strongest form of 'existence not implied', which the rule classes N, not grounds for omission. Dispute 4 (clock, load-bearing D): the analyst's extraction-based D-justification is rejected with the audit; the audit's alternative N-horn is also rejected (no standard presentation mints an internal clock, and an unrecursed clock would imply nothing); refiled as T — a model-side, pure-gauge indexing choice with no internal content and no eliminator, hence not an implication source; contributes 0 in every reading. Undisputed data 4, 6, 8, 9 upheld as P. Final: D(15) = 3.
